questions.text: Compound E, C3H8(g), reacts with oxygen, O2(g), according to the balanced equation: C3H8(g) + 5O2(g) → 3CO2(g) + 4H2O(g). Initially 8 cm³ of compound E and 50 cm³ of oxygen were injected into a container of adjustable volume and allowed to react. [Diagram: sealed syringe-like container holding the reaction mixture.] 2.3.1 Write down the name for this type of reaction.
Calculate the TOTAL volume of the GASES present in the container at the end of the reaction.
questions.memo_answer: Total volume of gases = 66 cm³ (or 0,066 dm³)
questions.memo_working: V(O2) used = 5V(C3H8) = (5)(8) = 40 cm³. V(CO2) formed = 3V(C3H8) = (3)(8) = 24 cm³. V(H2O) formed = 4V(C3H8) = (4)(8) = 32 cm³. V(O2) unused = 50 − 40 = 10 cm³. Total volume of gas in the container = 10 + 24 + 32 = 66 cm³. Marking criteria: (a) volume O2 and C3H8 used; (b) volume CO2 and H2O produced; (c) volume O2 remaining; (d) addition of the three volumes; (e) correct final answer 66 cm³ or 0,066 dm³. (Mole-based calculations using Vm = 22,4 dm³ also accepted.)

questions.text: Define the term reaction rate.
questions.memo_answer: Change in concentration of products/reactants per (unit) time. (Also accepted: change in amount/number of moles/volume/mass of products or reactants per (unit) time; amount/number of moles/volume/mass of products formed / reactants used per (unit) time; rate of change in concentration/amount/number of moles/volume/mass (2 or 0).)
questions.memo_note: Memo note: give the mark for 'per unit time' only if in context of reaction rate.

questions.text: Carbon monoxide, CO(g), reacts with oxygen, O2(g), to form carbon dioxide, CO2(g), in a sealed container according to the balanced equation: 2CO(g) + O2(g) → 2CO2(g). The graph below shows the concentration of O2(g) versus time. [Graph of concentration of O2(g) (mol·dm⁻³) versus time (s): the curve starts at 0,27 mol·dm⁻³ (between the 0,25 and 0,30 gridlines) at t = 0, falls steeply to 0,15 mol·dm⁻³ at 10 s, continues falling less steeply and flattens to 0,05 mol·dm⁻³ from about 40 s to 60 s; axis gridlines at 0,05 intervals from 0 to 0,30 and at 10 s intervals from 0 to 60.] 5.2.1 At which time, 10 s or 30 s, is the reaction rate higher?
The reaction takes place in a 3 dm³ container. Calculate the average rate (in mol·s⁻¹) at which CO2(g) is formed in the first 10 s.
questions.memo_working: Rate = −Δc(O2)/Δt = −(0,15 − 0,27)/(10 − 0) = 0,012 mol·dm⁻³·s⁻¹. Rate(O2) in mol·s⁻¹ = cV = (0,012)(3) = 0,036 mol·s⁻¹. Rate(CO2) = 2 x rate(O2) = 2 x 0,036 = 0,072 mol·s⁻¹. Marking criteria: (a) calculate the change [O2]final − [O2]initial (accept 0,265 to 0,27 for [O2]initial); (b) substitute 10 s in rate formula; (c) multiply rate/concentration of O2 by 3 dm³; (d) use mole ratio n(O2) : n(CO2) = 1 : 2; (e) final correct answer 0,072 mol·s⁻¹.

questions.text: Equilibrium is established at 25 °C in a saturated calcium hydroxide solution according to the reaction: Ca(OH)2(s) ⇌ Ca2+(aq) + 2OH⁻(aq). State Le Chatelier's principle.
questions.memo_answer: When the equilibrium in a closed system is disturbed, the system will re-instate a new equilibrium by favouring the reaction that will cancel/oppose the disturbance.
questions.memo_note: Memo instruction: if any one of the underlined key phrases in the correct context is omitted, deduct 1 mark.

questions.text: A few drops of concentrated hydrochloric acid, HCℓ(conc.), are added to the equilibrium mixture. What effect does this addition have on the mass of Ca(OH)2(s)? Choose from INCREASES, DECREASES or REMAINS THE SAME.
Explain the answer to QUESTION 6.1.2 by using Le Chatelier's principle.
questions.memo_answer: The decrease in the amount/concentration of OH⁻ ions favours the reaction that increases the amount/concentration of OH⁻ ions (OR the acid/HCℓ/H+ reacts with the OH⁻ ions); the forward reaction is favoured (OR the amount/concentration of the products increases).

questions.text: Initially 70 g of NH4HS(s) is placed in a 3 dm³ container at 250 °C. The container is sealed and the reaction is allowed to reach equilibrium according to the balanced equation: NH4HS(s) ⇌ NH3(g) + H2S(g). The Kc values for the decomposition of NH4HS(s) at different temperatures are given in the table below. [Table: 200 °C - Kc = 7,5 x 10⁻²; 250 °C - Kc = 18 x 10⁻²; 300 °C - Kc = 40 x 10⁻².] 6.2.1 Is the decomposition of NH4HS(s) an EXOTHERMIC or ENDOTHERMIC reaction?
Explain the answer to QUESTION 6.2.1 by using Le Chatelier's principle.
questions.memo_answer: With an increase in the temperature the Kc value increases; the concentration of the products increases (OR concentration of reactants decreases OR the forward reaction is favoured); (according to Le Chatelier's principle) an increase in temperature favours the endothermic reaction.

questions.text: Calculate the mass of NH4HS(s) that will be present at equilibrium at 250 °C.
questions.memo_answer: m(NH4HS) at equilibrium ≈ 5,61 g [memo's stated answer; accepted RANGE: 4,96 - 5,74 g; Option 1 of the memo itself obtains 5,1 g]
questions.memo_working: n(NH4HS) initial = m/M = 70/51 = 1,37 mol. Since NH4HS is a solid it is omitted from Kc: Kc = [NH3][H2S]. Let x mol decompose (ratio NH4HS : NH3 : H2S = 1 : 1 : 1); equilibrium concentrations [NH3] = [H2S] = x/3 (3 dm³ container). 18 x 10⁻² = (x/3)²; x = 1,27 mol. n(NH4HS) at equilibrium = 1,37 − 1,27 = 0,1 mol; m = nM = 0,1 x 51 = 5,1 g. (Option 2, working in concentrations: x = 0,42 mol·dm⁻³ so n(change) = 1,26 mol, m(eq) = 0,11 x 51 = 5,61 g or 70 − 64,26 = 5,74 g; concentration route gives 4,998 - 5,128 g. Hence the accepted range 4,96 - 5,74 g.) Marking criteria: (a) n(NH4HS) = 70/51; (b) ratio 1:1:1; (c) equilibrium concentrations (divide equilibrium moles by 3); (d) correct Kc expression; (e) substitute Kc = 18 x 10⁻²; (f) n(NH4HS)eq = n(in) − n(change); (g) substitute 51 in n = m/M; (h) correct final answer. No Kc expression with correct substitution: max 7/8; wrong Kc expression: max 6/8.

questions.text: Phosphoric acid, H3PO4(aq), is an example of an acid that can ionise in three steps, as shown below: H3PO4(aq) + H2O(ℓ) ⇌ H3O+(aq) + H2PO4⁻(aq), Ka = 6,9 x 10⁻³; H2PO4⁻(aq) + H2O(ℓ) ⇌ H3O+(aq) + HPO4²⁻(aq), Ka = 6,2 x 10⁻⁸; HPO4²⁻(aq) + H2O(ℓ) ⇌ H3O+(aq) + PO4³⁻(aq), Ka = 4,8 x 10⁻¹³. 7.1.1 Which one is the stronger acid, H2PO4⁻ or HPO4²⁻? Give a reason for the answer by referring to the data above.
questions.memo_answer: H2PO4⁻. The Ka of H2PO4⁻ is greater/higher than the Ka of HPO4²⁻. (Accept: Ka of H2PO4⁻ greater.)

questions.text: Barium hydroxide, Ba(OH)2, dissolves in water according to the balanced equation: Ba(OH)2(s) → Ba2+(aq) + 2OH⁻(aq). A 100 cm³ solution is prepared by dissolving an unknown amount of Ba(OH)2 at 25 °C. 25 cm³ of this Ba(OH)2 solution is reacted with 15 cm³ of a 0,2 mol·dm⁻³ HCℓ solution in a flask, according to the balanced equation: Ba(OH)2(aq) + 2HCℓ(aq) → BaCℓ2(aq) + 2H2O(ℓ). The final pH of the solution is 12,62 at 25 °C. Calculate the final concentration of the hydroxide ions in the flask.
questions.memo_working: Option 1: pH = −log[H3O+]; 12,62 = −log[H3O+]; [H3O+] = 2,4 x 10⁻¹³ mol·dm⁻³. [H3O+][OH⁻] = 10⁻¹⁴; (2,4 x 10⁻¹³)[OH⁻] = 1 x 10⁻¹⁴; [OH⁻] = 0,0417 mol·dm⁻³. Option 2: pH + pOH = 14; pOH = 1,38; pOH = −log[OH⁻]; [OH⁻] = 0,042 mol·dm⁻³. Criteria: (a) any correct formula; (b) substitute 12,62; (c) substitute the calculated [H3O+] in [H3O+][OH⁻] (or 1,38 in pOH = −log[OH⁻]); (d) final answer.

questions.text: Calculate the number of moles of Ba(OH)2 used to prepare the 100 cm³ solution.
questions.memo_answer: n(Ba(OH)2) = 9,34 x 10⁻³ mol [accepted RANGE: 9,2 x 10⁻³ - 9,36 x 10⁻³ mol]
questions.memo_working: POSITIVE MARKING FROM QUESTION 7.2.1. n(HCℓ) = cV = (0,2)(0,015) = 3 x 10⁻³ mol. n(OH⁻) reacted = n(HCℓ) = 3 x 10⁻³ mol (1:1). n(OH⁻) remaining = cV = (0,0417)(0,04) = 1,67 x 10⁻³ mol (total volume in the flask = 25 + 15 = 40 cm³). n(OH⁻) initial = 3 x 10⁻³ + 1,67 x 10⁻³ = 4,67 x 10⁻³ mol. n(Ba(OH)2) = ½ n(OH⁻) = ½(4,67 x 10⁻³) = 2,33 x 10⁻³ mol in 25 cm³. In 100 cm³: (4)(2,33 x 10⁻³) = 9,34 x 10⁻³ mol. Criteria: (a) substitute 0,2 mol·dm⁻³ and 0,015 dm³ in n = cV; (b) use ratio n(OH⁻):n(HCℓ) = 1:1 or n(Ba(OH)2):n(HCℓ) = 1:2; (c) substitute c(OH⁻) and 0,04 in n = cV; (d) n(OH⁻)initial = n(reacted) + n(final); (e) use ratio n(Ba(OH)2):n(OH⁻) = 1:2; (f) multiply by 4 (or divide by 0,025 dm³ and multiply by 0,1 dm³); (g) final answer.

questions.text: The diagram below represents a cell that operates initially under standard conditions. [Diagram: galvanic cell with a voltmeter V connecting an Aℓ electrode in Aℓ3+(aq) solution and a Zn electrode in Zn2+(aq) solution, joined by a salt bridge.] 8.1 Define the term electrolyte.
questions.memo_answer: A substance whose (aqueous) solution contains ions (2 or 0) / a substance that dissolves in water to give a solution that conducts electricity (through movement of ions) / a substance that dissociates to form ions in water / in molten state.

questions.text: Which ion concentration, Aℓ3+(aq) or Zn2+(aq), will increase? Give a reason for the answer.
questions.memo_answer: Aℓ3+/aluminium ion. Aℓ is oxidised OR Aℓ is a stronger reducing agent.

questions.text: Write down the cell notation for this cell.
questions.memo_answer: Aℓ(s) | Aℓ3+(aq) || Zn2+(aq) | Zn(s). (Also accepted with concentrations 1 mol·dm⁻³, or without phases: Aℓ | Aℓ3+ || Zn2+ | Zn.)

questions.text: The electrolyte in the aluminium half-cell is prepared by dissolving some aluminium sulphate, Aℓ2(SO4)3(s), in water. Calculate the mass of Aℓ2(SO4)3(s) needed to prepare 250 cm³ of this solution so that the cell operates initially under STANDARD CONDITIONS.
questions.memo_working: Standard conditions: [Aℓ3+] = 1 mol·dm⁻³. n(Aℓ3+) = cV = (1)(0,25) = 0,25 mol. n(Aℓ2(SO4)3) = ½ n(Aℓ3+) = ½(0,25) = 0,125 mol. m = nM = 0,125 x 342 = 42,75 g. Criteria: (a) calculate n(Aℓ3+); (b) use mole ratio n(Aℓ2(SO4)3) : n(Aℓ3+) = 1 : 2; (c) multiply n(Aℓ2(SO4)3) by M = 342; (d) final correct answer 42,75 g.

questions.text: The diagram below represents a cell used for the refining of copper. [Diagram: cell connected to a power source (battery symbol) with electrode Q and electrode R immersed in an electrolyte.] The unrefined copper contains zinc as the only impurity. 9.1 Is this an ELECTROLYTIC or a GALVANIC cell?

When the switch is closed, it is found after T hours that the amount of Cu2+(aq) ions in the electrolyte changed by 0,05 moles and 0,15 moles of Cu(s) were deposited on electrode Q. How will the concentration of the zinc ions in the electrolyte be affected during the refining of the copper? Choose from INCREASES, DECREASES or REMAINS THE SAME.
Will the amount of Cu2+(aq) ions INCREASE or DECREASE? Explain the answer in terms of the relative strengths of the oxidising agents present.
questions.memo_answer: Decrease. More copper(II) ions/Cu2+ are reduced than formed / only copper(II) ions/Cu2+ are reduced; the copper(II) ion/Cu2+ is a stronger oxidising agent than the zinc(II) ion/Zn2+ (OR Zn2+ is a weaker oxidising agent than Cu2+).

questions.text: Calculate the change in mass of electrode R after T hours.
questions.memo_answer: Change in mass of electrode R = 9,6 g (decrease in mass). (NO RANGE)
questions.memo_working: Electrode R is the impure copper anode. n(Zn2+) formed = n(Cu2+) decrease = 0,05 mol; m(Zn) = nM = (0,05)(65) = 3,25 g Zn lost from R. Cu oxidised at R = 0,15 − 0,05 = 0,1 mol; m(Cu) = nM = 0,1(63,5) = 6,35 g Cu lost from R. Change in mass = 6,35 + 3,25 = 9,6 g (decrease). Criteria: (a) use ratio n(Cu2+) : n(Zn2+) = 1 : 1; (b) formula n = m/M; (c) substitute 65 and n(Zn2+); (d) subtraction of moles; (e) substitute 63,5 and n(Cu); (f) final correct answer 9,6 g.
